newsitem.title: UK: Boots chief says EMU in 1999 looks doubtful.
newsitem.headline: Boots chief says EMU in 1999 looks doubtful.

text.p: Boots Co Plc chairman Sir Michael Angus said developments in France and Germany over the past week suggested European Monetary Union might be delayed beyond the current 1999 deadline.
"It's in a very fluid state," Angus said at a news conference on Boots annual results.

The monetary union timetable has been called into question after the Socialist victory in the French elections at the weekend and the row between Germany's finance minister Theo Waigel and the Bundesbank over the government's plan to use gold reserves to help Germany qualify for the single currency.

Angus said while companies had to be prepared for monetary union, he doubted there would be support for it if criteria for joining the single currency were fudged. "Not many people want to go into EMU with a total fudge."
Boots' deputy chairman and chief executive Lord Blyth said he doubted very much Britain would join the single currency in the first wave.
"I wouldn't think there's a hope in hell we'll be in it in the first wave."

Blyth said he thought the single currency would inevitably be inflationary and the cost to retailers of implementing it would be twice as much as adapting computer systems to cope with the Millenium bug, which he estimated in Boots' case at around 10 million stg.
